What is Seobot?

Seobot is an SEO research site and free SEO check. It measures how Google and AI search crawlers read the web — starting with a two-pass crawl of 1,700 top sites — and turns the findings into a prioritized fix list for your own site.

Built on the research

The study, running on your site

This study asked two questions of 1,700 top sites: does a non-rendering AI crawler receive the page, and do the robots.txt rules let AI search in? The free SEO check asks the same of yours — and the dashboard visualizes the answers.

Machine readability

See how much of your page a non-rendering AI crawler actually receives — raw HTML versus the rendered page, scored the same way this study scored 1,700 top sites.

AI crawler access

Your robots.txt, checked token by token against GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot — so AI search is blocked on purpose, never by accident.

Data visualizations

Interactive heatmaps, radar charts, and flow diagrams showing crawler blocking patterns, anti-bot barriers by vertical, JSON-LD structured data, and raw vs. rendered content gaps.

Linked explorer

Every one of 1,700 crawled sites as a dot you can re-arrange by rank, vertical, outcome, or any measured metric — then filter by crawler policy, structured data, CDN, CMS, and agent-readiness. Every view is a shareable link.

Best practices scorecard

How many studied sites pass each measurable SEO and GEO ranking factor, with the sample size behind every rate and a label for whether the test is direct or a proxy.

A page for every site

Per-crawler robots.txt verdicts, raw-versus-rendered content metrics, and an SEO and GEO deep dive for each of the 1,700 sites crawled — readable or not.

FAQ

Questions, answered

The research, the free SEO check, and the data behind both. Email support@seobot.io — a human replies within a day.

Seobot is an SEO research site. It publishes a sourced study of how Google and AI crawlers read 1,700 top websites, and a free two-minute SEO check that turns those findings into a prioritized fix list for your own site.

We crawled 1,700 homepages from Tranco list 64VVX with the same user agent: once over plain HTTP and once in headless Chromium (the first 500 twice, to test stability), and kept going down the list until 1,025 were readable. JavaScript execution is the only variable, so the gap between the passes shows what a non-rendering AI crawler misses.

About 15 questions across Search Console, indexing, content, links, speed, and AI visibility. Two come straight from the study: whether your content survives without JavaScript, and whether your robots.txt and firewall let AI search crawlers in. Each answer becomes a fix or a verify step, ranked by impact.

No. The check runs entirely in your browser, with nothing to install and no account to create. You answer about 15 plain-English questions, and the score is calculated on your device. The URL you enter only personalizes the report and prefills links to Google's own tools. Nothing is fetched or stored.

Each answer scores Yes = 1, Not sure = 0.5, or No = 0, weighted by how much the issue matters and by your site type. “Not sure” lowers the report's confidence rather than counting as a failure. There are no industry benchmarks, because we only publish numbers we have measured.

Yes. The first-party study data is licensed CC BY 4.0, so you can reuse and republish it with attribution to Seobot. Third-party sources keep their own licenses and are cited rather than republished.
